items.stem: In which year did Braj Kachru publish his model of the three concentric circles of English?
items.markingKey: Kachru’s model appeared in 1985.

items.stem: Explain why Egypt is placed in Kachru’s expanding circle, and what this suggests about the status of English there.
items.answer: English is learnt as a foreign language, mainly for international communication (norm-dependent).

items.stem: Explain why New Zealand is placed in Kachru’s inner circle, and what this suggests about the status of English there.

items.stem: A survey of a small island language in Lisbon recorded the percentage of each age group who speak it fluently: 60+: 84%; 40–59: 56%; 20–39: 39%; under 20: 26%. (a) Calculate the difference in percentage points between the oldest and youngest groups. (b) Calculate the percentage decrease in fluency rate from the oldest to the youngest group.
items.answer: (a) 84 − 26 = 58 percentage points. (b) (26 − 84) ÷ 84 × 100 = -69.0%, a decrease of 69.0%.
items.markingKey: Award up to 2 marks: (a) 58 percentage points; (b) 69.0% decrease with method.

items.stem: A survey of a mountain community’s language in Karachi recorded the percentage of each age group who speak it fluently: 60+: 85%; 40–59: 63%; 20–39: 40%; under 20: 10%. (a) Calculate the difference in percentage points between the oldest and youngest groups. (b) Calculate the percentage decrease in fluency rate from the oldest to the youngest group. (c) Explain what the data suggest about the future of the language.
items.answer: (a) 85 − 10 = 75 percentage points. (b) (10 − 85) ÷ 85 × 100 = -88.2%, a decrease of 88.2%. (c) Intergenerational transmission is breaking down; without intervention the language is heading towards endangerment or death.
items.markingKey: Award up to 3 marks: (a) 75 percentage points; (b) 88.2% decrease with method; (c) interpretation linked to intergenerational transmission and stages of endangerment.

items.stem: Explain how the internet has contributed to the global spread of English.
items.answer: English dominates much online content and platforms, and online communication spreads new forms quickly.

items.stem: This exchange took place during a phone call between a supplier and a buyer; neither speaker has English as a first language: Mohammed: ‘She work in a bank in Frankfurt.’ Zara: ‘Let’s make a discussion on Monday.’ Analyse the ELF features and evaluate whether they would affect communication.
items.answer: ‘She work in a bank in Frankfurt.’: dropping third-person -s – a common ELF feature that rarely causes misunderstanding. ‘Let’s make a discussion on Monday.’: overuse of common verbs – ‘make’ used with a wide range of nouns. Meaning remains clear, so communication is likely to succeed.
items.markingKey: Award up to 2 marks, 1 per valid point: ‘She work in a bank in Frankfurt.’ – dropping third-person -s: a common ELF feature that rarely causes misunderstanding; ‘Let’s make a discussion on Monday.’ – overuse of common verbs: ‘make’ used with a wide range of nouns; evaluation: intelligibility rather than native-speaker correctness; reference to ELF research (Jenkins, Seidlhofer).

items.stem: This exchange took place during an online meeting between engineers in two different countries; neither speaker has English as a first language: Mateo: ‘This is the man which I met.’ Yusuf: ‘You are coming tomorrow, isn’t it?’ Analyse the ELF features and evaluate whether they would affect communication.
items.answer: ‘This is the man which I met.’: interchangeable who/which – relative pronouns used without the human/non-human distinction. ‘You are coming tomorrow, isn’t it?’: invariant tag question – one tag used for all statements. Meaning remains clear, so communication is likely to succeed.

items.stem: A survey of a coastal fishing community’s language in Manila recorded the percentage of each age group who speak it fluently: 60+: 91%; 40–59: 71%; 20–39: 55%; under 20: 38%. (a) Calculate the difference in percentage points between the oldest and youngest groups. (b) Calculate the percentage decrease in fluency rate from the oldest to the youngest group.
items.answer: (a) 91 − 38 = 53 percentage points. (b) (38 − 91) ÷ 91 × 100 = -58.2%, a decrease of 58.2%.
items.markingKey: Award up to 2 marks: (a) 53 percentage points; (b) 58.2% decrease with method.
